h: Raising the Lamps to Transform Darkness Into Light

p: In the holy Zohar at the beginning of this parshah:
'And it is like a groom coming out of his canopy,' etc.
that is, the aspect of Atika;
what is said, "And it is like a groom":
with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding";
and that is Binah, the supernal mother.
"This is the head of all light,
'From the end of the heavens is its going forth'";
which is the end of the heavens Above,
the Hidden Intellect beyond all thought.
And this is the order of the middle line:
the aspect of the Oral Torah.
and these are the seven attributes,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַגָּהַת רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל
as written in the gloss of Rabbi Chaim Vital
And there in the holy Zohar:
to be lit by the Kohen."
And the holy Zohar comes to explain
was to draw down the holiness
to the attribute of Malchus, Bas Sheva,
shall the seven lamps give light,"
and Rashi explained, from the Sifrei,
that all of them should face the middle one;
and the commentators, of blessed memory, asked:
that "God made one opposite the other" (Koheles 7:14);
and opposite the seven attributes of holiness
which are also comprised of ten
and they are the husk of the seventy nations,
the leaven in the dough in the heart.
And this is what is said,
that stand opposite the face of the Menorah,
and they will repair all the corruption.
And it is written with the term "shall give light,"
"Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah," etc.,
"to love and to fear Your Name":
And this is what is said:
toward the face of the Menorah
that he raised up the lamps
the Hidden Intellect beyond all thought;
he also repaired "toward the face of the Menorah,"
which is the deeds of the wicked
from the six days of Creation
and this is so that the light will be
"that which comes out of the darkness"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
(as written in the holy Zohar, II 184a),
and then "they shall be white as snow,"
And this is what is said: "And Aharon did so,"
to make known the praise of Aharon,
for Aharon, the holy one of Hashem,
that he did not transgress Hashem's command?
and this is a great praise for Aharon,
also "toward the face of the Menorah,"
which are the seven attributes of the husk.
And Shabbos is the time for this rectification,
for Shabbos is the attribute of Malchus,
it is the crown of Malchus";
and they are able to repair
And this is what it said:
